chapters.title: Anatomy of the Aortic Valve Complex and Aortic Root
chapters.description: Detailed anatomical description of the aortic valve apparatus, aortic root and spatial relationships to the coronary ostia and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) relevant to valve interventions.
subtopics: Aortic valve cusps, commissures and annulus structure
Aortic root components: sinuses of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, ascending aorta
Coronary ostia anatomy and variability (height, orientation, takeoff)
Left ventricular outflow tract anatomy and dimensions
Spatial relationships between native valve, prosthetic frames and coronaries
Anatomical variants relevant to transcatheter interventions (calcification distribution, bicuspid anatomy)

chapters.title: Physiology and Hemodynamics of the Aortic Valve
chapters.description: Principles of normal and abnormal aortic valve hemodynamics, and the Doppler-echocardiographic and catheter-based parameters used to quantify valve function.
subtopics: Flow dynamics across the aortic valve and pressure–flow relationships
Transvalvular gradients and their determinants
Effective orifice area (EOA) and indexed EOA
Continuity equation and its application to AVA calculation
Doppler velocity index (DVI) and interpretation
Impact of prosthesis design and position on hemodynamics
Concepts of prosthesis–patient mismatch (PPM)

chapters.title: Pathophysiology of Aortic Stenosis and Bioprosthetic Valve Degeneration
chapters.description: Mechanisms leading to native aortic stenosis and structural valve deterioration of bioprosthetic valves, including mechanical, biological and infectious contributors.
subtopics: Degenerative (calcific) aortic stenosis mechanisms
Structural valve deterioration (SVD): leaflet calcification, fibrosis, tearing and pannus
Bioprosthetic valve thrombosis vs structural degeneration
Impact of leaflet design (supra- vs intra-annular) on durability
Role of infection (prosthetic valve endocarditis) in accelerated degeneration
Clinical and hemodynamic manifestations of valve failure (stenosis, regurgitation, mixed)

chapters.title: Infective Endocarditis: Principles and Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis (PVE)
chapters.description: Foundations of infective endocarditis including pathogenesis, causative organisms, diagnostic approach, and specific considerations for infection involving prosthetic valves.
subtopics: Microbiology: common pathogens (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Enterococcus) and their clinical implications
Pathogenesis of endocardial infection and vegetation formation
Clinical features and complications of IE and PVE
Diagnostic criteria: blood cultures, echocardiography (TTE/TEE) and ancillary imaging
Medical treatment principles and antibiotic regimens for common organisms (eg, Enterococcus spp.)
Indications and timing for surgical intervention in PVE
Long-term management, relapse risk and role of suppressive therapy

chapters.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI): Devices and Design Principles
chapters.description: Overview of TAVI device types, structural designs, and how design features influence implantation strategy, hemodynamics and complications.
subtopics: Device classifications: self-expanding, balloon-expandable, mechanically expandable
Valve frame architecture, skirt/ sealing mechanisms and leaflet positions (supra- vs intra-annular)
Examples of device-specific features affecting coronary access and frame height
Radial force, conformability to anatomy and interaction with calcified annuli
Clinical implications of frame height, cell design and commissural alignment

chapters.title: Valve-in-Valve and Repeat Transcatheter Interventions: Concepts and Techniques
chapters.description: Principles of performing valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures, indications for repeat TAVI, technical challenges and considerations unique to layered prostheses.
subtopics: Indications for ViV versus surgical re-replacement
Anatomical and hemodynamic implications of nested valve frames
Sizing strategies using surgical internal diameter (S-ID) and true internal diameter
Risks specific to ViV: coronary obstruction, elevated gradients, PPM
Strategies to optimize effective orifice area (high implant, supra-annular valves)
Planning for potential future coronary access in ViV contexts

chapters.title: Imaging for TAVI Planning: Multislice CT, Echocardiography and 3D Modeling
chapters.description: Imaging modalities and measurements required for preprocedural planning, intra-procedural guidance and postprocedural surveillance in transcatheter valve interventions.
subtopics: MSCT acquisition protocols for TAVI planning (ECG-gating, contrast timing)
Key CT measurements: annulus dimensions, perimeter, area, leaflet length, sinus diameters, coronary heights
Valve-to-coronary (VTC) distance and concepts for ViV planning
Assessment of prior prosthesis: internal lumen, frame geometry, leaflet position
Role of TEE and TTE: structural assessment, vegetation detection, hemodynamic quantification
3D reconstructions, virtual valve implantation and simulation tools
Limitations and artifacts in CT and echocardiography for prosthetic valves

chapters.title: Procedural Techniques in TAVI: Access, Deployment and Adjunctive Maneuvers
chapters.description: Operational steps and common interventional techniques used during TAVI, including vascular access strategies, rapid pacing, pre- and post-dilation, and device deployment methods.
subtopics: Vascular access options: transfemoral, transradial, alternative routes
Sheath selection and percutaneous closure devices
Use of rapid ventricular pacing and its indications
Balloon valvuloplasty (pre- and post-dilation): indications and sizing
Guidewire selection and positioning (eg, LV support wires)
Deployment techniques for self-expanding vs balloon-expandable valves
Techniques for commissural alignment during deployment

chapters.title: Risk of Coronary Obstruction in TAVI and Mitigation Strategies
chapters.description: Mechanisms of coronary obstruction during ViV and TAVI procedures, risk assessment, and prophylactic and rescue strategies to preserve coronary flow.
subtopics: Pathophysiology of coronary obstruction in native and prosthetic valve settings
Anatomic predictors: low coronary heights, small sinuses, narrow VTC
Preprocedural risk stratification using CT-based metrics
Coronary protection techniques: guidewire protection, pre-positioned balloons/stents (chimney technique)
Leaflet laceration (BASILICA): principles, indications and technical steps
Rescue strategies and immediate management of coronary compromise

chapters.title: Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture and Leaflet Modification Techniques
chapters.description: Rationale, mechanisms and procedural aspects of bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) and leaflet modification techniques used to improve hemodynamics in ViV procedures.
subtopics: Principles of bioprosthetic valve fracture and applicable valve types
Balloon selection, inflation pressures and timing relative to valve deployment
Hemodynamic effects and risks (annular injury, aortic root complications)
Leaflet modification procedures (eg, intentional laceration) and indications
Clinical evidence, outcomes and limitations of BVF/BASILICA in repeat interventions

chapters.title: Complications of TAVI and Repeat Valve Interventions
chapters.description: Overview of early and late complications associated with TAVI and redo procedures, their recognition, prevention and management.
subtopics: Vascular complications: dissection, perforation, pseudoaneurysm and hematoma
Bleeding risks and access-site management
Paravalvular leak: mechanisms, assessment and percutaneous closure options
Valve malposition, embolization and coronary obstruction
Conduction disturbances, new bundle branch block and need for permanent pacing
Acute kidney injury, stroke and infection risks
Long-term complications: structural deterioration, leaflet thrombosis, endocarditis

chapters.title: Conduction System Disturbances and Pacing Considerations Post-TAVI
chapters.description: Mechanisms of conduction injury during valve implantation, predictors of pacemaker requirement, and management strategies for postprocedural bradyarrhythmias.
subtopics: Anatomical basis for conduction disturbances after aortic valve interventions
Incidence and predictors of high-degree AV block and new pacemaker implantation
Device-specific rates and risk stratification
Intra-procedural monitoring and temporary pacing strategies
Indications for permanent pacemaker post-TAVI and pacing modes
Long-term implications of pacing on ventricular function and outcomes

chapters.title: Pharmacology Relevant to Endocarditis and Post-TAVI Care
chapters.description: Key pharmacologic agents and regimens used in the treatment of infective endocarditis, peri- and post-TAVI antithrombotic strategies, and heart failure guideline-directed medical therapy.
subtopics: Antimicrobial regimens for common IE pathogens (eg, Enterococcus spp.): beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, combination therapy alternatives
Indications and duration of intravenous versus oral therapy in PVE
Antiplatelet and anticoagulant strategies after TAVI (single vs dual therapy, indications based on AF/PCI)
Management of antithrombotic therapy around procedures and bleeding risk considerations
Heart failure pharmacotherapy relevant to valve disease (ACE inhibitors/ARBs, beta-blockers, MRAs, SGLT2 inhibitors)
Antibiotic prophylaxis principles for prosthetic valves and dental procedures

chapters.title: Hemodynamic Assessment and Echocardiographic Interpretation after Valve Interventions
chapters.description: Principles for interpreting echocardiographic findings after TAVI/ViV, assessing valve function, distinguishing prosthesis-patient mismatch from true stenosis, and monitoring over time.
subtopics: Doppler assessment of transvalvular gradients and velocity profiles post-implantation
Calculation and interpretation of EOA, indexed EOA and DVI in prosthetic valves
Criteria for patient–prosthesis mismatch and clinical significance
Echocardiographic surveillance schedule and key endpoints
Differentiating structural valve deterioration, thrombosis and paravalvular leak on imaging
Role of CT and TEE in ambiguous cases

chapters.title: Coronary Artery Disease Management in the Setting of Structural Aortic Valve Interventions
chapters.description: Integration of coronary artery disease (CAD) management with planning and performance of TAVI, addressing prior PCI, timing of revascularization, and considerations for future coronary access.
subtopics: Timing of PCI relative to TAVI (staged vs concurrent strategies)
Impact of prosthesis design and commissural alignment on future coronary access
Techniques to preserve or restore coronary access after valve implantation
Assessment of coronary anatomy in pre-TAVI CT
Management of ischemic symptoms after ViV and redo TAVI

chapters.title: Surgical Considerations, Risk Scores and Indications for Operative Management
chapters.description: Principles guiding the decision between surgical and transcatheter approaches for valve dysfunction and endocarditis, including risk stratification tools and operative considerations.
subtopics: Risk scoring systems: EuroSCORE II, STS score and their applications
Indications for surgical valve replacement in native and prosthetic valve endocarditis
Technical challenges of explanting transcatheter valves and root replacement scenarios
Comparative outcomes of surgical vs transcatheter reintervention in high-risk patients
Operative perioperative considerations in frail and comorbid patients

chapters.title: Lifetime Management of Patients with Bioprosthetic Aortic Valves
chapters.description: Framework for long-term planning from index valve implantation through potential reinterventions, focusing on prosthesis selection, surveillance and strategies to preserve future options.
subtopics: Patient-centered planning: age, comorbidities and expected longevity
Choosing prosthesis type with future re-intervention in mind (frame height, commissural markers)
Surveillance protocols and triggers for reintervention
Strategies to minimize prosthesis–patient mismatch over time
Counseling patients about trade-offs and procedural trajectories

chapters.title: CT-Based 3D Modeling and Simulation for Procedural Planning
chapters.description: Use of advanced CT-based 3D reconstruction and virtual implantation tools to predict interactions between devices, estimate coronary risk and optimize device selection and implant depth.
subtopics: Workflow for CT segmentation and 3D model generation
Virtual valve deployment simulation and prediction of neo-skirt and leaflet position
Quantification of valve-to-coronary distances and predicted obstruction
Limitations of simulation and integration with fluoroscopic planning
Examples of how modeling informs choice of valve type and implant depth

chapters.title: Ethical, Multidisciplinary Decision-Making and Informed Consent in Complex Valvular Interventions
chapters.description: Principles of multidisciplinary team (heart team) decision-making, shared decision-making with patients and families, and ethical considerations in high-risk or off-label interventions.
subtopics: Structure and roles of the heart team in valvular disease management
Frameworks for weighing risks and benefits in high-risk reinterventions
Documentation and informed consent for off-label device use
Palliative considerations and patient goals of care in structural heart disease
Regulatory and institutional governance for novel or complex procedures

chapters.title: Epidemiology and Outcomes of TAVI, Valve-in-Valve, and Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
chapters.description: Population-level data about the prevalence, outcomes and long-term durability of transcatheter aortic valve therapies and the incidence and prognosis of PVE.
subtopics: Trends in TAVI use across risk strata and age groups
Durability data and rates of structural valve deterioration after TAVI versus surgical bioprostheses
Incidence, risk factors and outcomes of prosthetic valve endocarditis
Reported outcomes of valve-in-valve and repeat transcatheter procedures
Knowledge gaps and areas of active research
